RAGING HUNTER
INSTRUCTION MANUAL — Rev. 8 (UNKNOWN — not printed in the document)
cleanIntro: The Raging Hunter book covers five chamberings under one name - 357H, 44H, 454H, 460H and 500H - and the .44 Magnum 44H is a six-shot on an 8-3/8, 6-3/4 or 5-1/8 inch barrel with a fully adjustable rear sight. Two things set it apart at the bench: the cylinder needs BOTH the thumb piece and the front latch released at once, and Taurus forbids disassembling the barrel outright, which matters because the Raging Hunter's shrouded, rail-topped barrel looks like an assembly that comes apart.

steps.title: Confirm the chambering - five Raging Hunters share this book
steps.action: Check what is stamped on your barrel against the tables. The 44H is .44 Magnum, DA/SA, six rounds, on an 8-3/8, 6-3/4 or 5-1/8 inch barrel; the 454H beside it in the same table is .454 Casull and holds five, and the 357H, 460H and 500H are in the other tables again.
steps.prose: The capacity difference is the practical one for clearing: a 44H has six chambers and a 454H on the identical frame has five, so a habit built on the wrong table leaves a chamber unchecked. The correct cartridge is marked on the revolver, and that stamp is the authority - not the book, and not what was in the ammunition can.
steps.aside: Taurus does allow one substitution here: .44 Special ammunition may be fired in Taurus revolvers chambered for .44 Magnum. They also state these are the only caliber substitutions that will function and that attempting others can damage the firearm.
steps.cite:
RAGING HUNTER
INSTRUCTION MANUAL — Rev. 8 — Specifications, printed p.13 (PDF p.7)

steps.title: Two latches at once - thumb piece forward AND front latch down
steps.action: Muzzle safe, finger off the trigger. Push the thumb piece forward with your right thumb and at the same time press the front latch down with your left hand, then swing the cylinder out to the left. Look into all six chambers.
steps.prose: This is the Raging Hunter's signature and the thing that defeats owners coming from a normal double-action revolver: the cylinder is held at BOTH ends to survive .44 Magnum pressure, so releasing one latch does nothing. Both have to be off together, and the motion is forward on the thumb piece, down on the front latch. If it will not budge, you are almost certainly holding one of the two.
steps.quote: Revolver Be sure the firearm is completely unloaded and contains no cartridges or cartridge cases. With the thumb of the right hand push the thumb piece forward and simultaneously press down the front latch with the left hand. Then press on the cylinder to swing it to the left. Visually check that all six (6) chambers are empty.
steps.cite:
RAGING HUNTER
INSTRUCTION MANUAL — Rev. 8 — Firearms Safety Systems, printed p.9 (PDF p.5)

steps.title: Muzzle up and push the extractor rod hard
steps.action: With the cylinder fully out, point the barrel upward and press sharply on the extractor rod. Confirm every fired case has cleared before you go on.
steps.prose: A .44 Magnum case is long and, after a hot load, expanded hard against the chamber wall, so this stroke needs commitment - a tentative push lifts the cases half an inch and lets them drop straight back as the rod returns. Support the weight of the gun with the other hand: a 55-ounce revolver with a 8-3/8 inch barrel wants to nose over exactly when you are pushing upward.
steps.quote: Cartridges are then ejected by pressing sharply on the extractor rod. Be sure that all fired cartridges are ejected. The cylinder is now ready to be reloaded (Fig.4).
steps.cite:
RAGING HUNTER
INSTRUCTION MANUAL — Rev. 8 — Operating Instructions, printed p.22 (PDF p.12)
steps.warn: Spent cases will be hot and may have sharp edges. Exercise caution when removing the cases or injury may occur.

steps.title: Both latches again, then check every chamber
steps.action: Before cleaning: muzzle in a safe direction, finger off the trigger, thumb piece AND front latch depressed and the cylinder completely swung out, and every chamber checked to be certain the revolver holds no cartridges or cartridge cases.
steps.prose: Taurus repeats the dual-latch instruction in the cleaning section rather than referring back, which tells you how often it is the step people skip. The cylinder-out position is the working state for the whole clean; on a Raging Hunter there is nothing else to open, and the front latch means it is also the only position in which the cylinder is not under tension.
steps.quote: Before cleaning, (1) keep the muzzle pointed in a safe direction, (2) keep your finger off the trigger, (3) depress thumb piece and front latch and completely swing out the cylinder and complete, (4) check every chamber to ensure firearm is completely unloaded and contains no cartridges or cartridge cases.
steps.cite:
RAGING HUNTER
INSTRUCTION MANUAL — Rev. 8 — Care and Maintenance, printed p.25 (PDF p.13)

steps.title: The barrel does not come off - that is an instruction, not a caution
steps.action: Leave the barrel assembly alone. Taurus states the gun is cleaned and lubricated under normal conditions with no disassembly needed and then says, separately and in plain words, do not disassemble the barrel.
steps.prose: This deserves its own step on a Raging Hunter specifically. The barrel is a shrouded assembly with a Picatinny rail on top and visible fasteners along it, so it reads as something designed to come apart - it is not, and taking it down changes the barrel/cylinder relationship the revolver was headspaced with. If the barrel genuinely needs work, the book's route is the factory, a qualified gunsmith or the importer.
steps.quote: 1. The gun may be cleaned and lubricated under normal conditions without the need of any disassembly. Do not disassemble the barrel.
steps.cite:
RAGING HUNTER
INSTRUCTION MANUAL — Rev. 8 — Care and Maintenance, printed p.25 (PDF p.13)

steps.title: Rail hardware is variant-specific - check before you touch a screw
steps.action: Look at what your revolver actually carries. Taurus lists a top and lower Picatinny rail MIL-STD-1913 'where applicable', so some Raging Hunters have both rails and some have only the top one. Clean around whatever is fitted and leave its screws at the torque they came at.
steps.prose: This matters because a scope or a light on the top rail is the reason most Raging Hunters get cleaned at all, and a rail screw nipped up during a wipe-down loses a zero that took a box of .44 Magnum to establish. If an optic is mounted, clean around it; if it has to come off, note that the rear sight underneath is fully adjustable and is not a substitute reference.
steps.quote: Top & Lower Picatinny Rail MIL-STD-1913 (where applicable)
steps.cite:
RAGING HUNTER
INSTRUCTION MANUAL — Rev. 8 — Specifications, printed p.15 (PDF p.8)

steps.title: Sight adjustment is an external-adjustable job and not part of a clean
steps.action: If your Raging Hunter has the fully adjustable external rear sight, adjust it only deliberately and never as a side effect of cleaning. Taurus's procedure is: unloaded, muzzle safe, cylinder left open if possible, elevation screw counterclockwise to raise and clockwise to lower, windage screw clockwise to move the notch right.
steps.prose: The 44H's rear sight is listed as fully adjustable, so those screws are live on this gun - which is exactly why a cloth dragged across them at the bench can cost you a zero without a sound. Note the screws before you wipe, and if you do adjust, do it at the range against a target rather than in the workshop.
steps.quote: External Adjustable Sight Models Only To adjust, make sure the firearm is unloaded   and   always   keep   the muzzle pointed in a safe direction.
steps.cite:
RAGING HUNTER
INSTRUCTION MANUAL — Rev. 8 — Adjusting the Sights, printed p.24 (PDF p.13)

steps.title: Nothing here transfers to another big-bore revolver
steps.action: Take the dual-latch release as belonging to this gun. Taurus warns that firearms which look alike differ widely in design, operation and the location and function of their controls, and a front latch on the crane is a feature most large revolvers do not have at all.
steps.prose: The mistake in this direction is quiet: a shooter who owns both a Raging Hunter and a conventional .44 will eventually try to force one cylinder open with a single latch and conclude the gun is broken, or - worse - hunt for a front latch on a revolver that has none and lever at the ejector shroud instead.
steps.quote:
FIREARMS ARE NOT ALL ALIKE
Many makes and models of firearms might LOOK nearly the same. However, they differ widely in design, operation, and in the location and function of various controls.
steps.cite:
RAGING HUNTER
INSTRUCTION MANUAL — Rev. 8 — Ammunition, printed p.21 (PDF p.11)

steps.title: After shooting: powder out, lead scrubbed, clean before 200 rounds pass
steps.action: Clean after shooting rather than after storage. Remove all powder residue from the barrel and the areas around it with an appropriate brush, and if lead has built up in the barrel, scrub it with a brass brush drenched with oil, then lubricate as described. Clean before more than 200 rounds go through in a row.
steps.prose: The lead line is not generic on a .44 Magnum: cast bullets are common in this chambering and heavy loads strip lead into the forcing cone and the first inches of rifling faster than any jacketed load. A leaded bore raises pressure, and pressure in a .44 Magnum is not something to be casual about - which is also why the brush is brass and wet, not steel and dry.
steps.quote: 5. For cleaning after shooting, it is of special importance that all residues of powder be removed from barrel and other adjacent areas subject to such deposits, using an appropriate brush. If particles of lead are detected in barrel they must be scrubbed with a brass brush, drenched with oil.
steps.cite:
RAGING HUNTER
INSTRUCTION MANUAL — Rev. 8 — Care and Maintenance, printed p.25 (PDF p.13)

steps.title: Field strip complete - cylinder out and nothing else
steps.action: Cylinder swung out on both latches, all six chambers empty. That is the entire Raging Hunter field strip; no part of this revolver is removed for cleaning, and the barrel in particular stays where it is.
steps.prose: The exploded view in the back is a parts list without an order of operations. Taurus's stated route for anything that genuinely needs the gun opened is the factory, a qualified gunsmith or the importer - and on a revolver built around .44 Magnum pressures, the sideplate and the crane are not places to experiment.
steps.quote: 2. In special conditions, such as repairs, when disassembling is necessary, it is recommended the gun be returned to the factory or sent to a qualified gunsmith or to the importer.
steps.cite:
RAGING HUNTER
INSTRUCTION MANUAL — Rev. 8 — Care and Maintenance, printed p.25 (PDF p.13)

deepAbsentReason: The Raging Hunter book publishes no disassembly and forbids one specifically: 'The gun may be cleaned and lubricated under normal conditions without the need of any disassembly. Do not disassemble the barrel.' On this revolver that sentence has teeth, because the Raging Hunter's barrel is a shrouded assembly with a Picatinny rail on top of it, and it looks like something that comes apart. Taurus's next line sends any case where disassembly is genuinely necessary back to the factory, a qualified gunsmith or the importer. The exploded view is a parts list. There is no deeper procedure to walk.

cleaning.name: BORE, FORCING CONE & LEAD
tasks: Remove all powder residue from the barrel and the adjacent areas with an appropriate brush
If lead particles are detected in the barrel, scrub them out with a brass brush drenched with oil, then lubricate as described
Work the forcing cone deliberately - on a .44 Magnum it takes the worst of the lead and the gas cutting
On a long 8-3/8 inch barrel use a full-length rod and pull the brush right out at the muzzle each pass rather than reversing it inside the bore
Check the bore for light before the revolver goes away

cleaning.name: CHAMBERS, CYLINDER FACE & STAR
tasks: Brush all six chambers with solvent and follow with a dry patch; sticky .44 cases start as a carbon ring at the case mouth
Clear the carbon ring off the front face of the cylinder
Push the extractor rod back and clean behind the star - the long .44 rims trap debris there
Wipe the barrel/cylinder gap and check the topstrap above it for flame cutting

cleaning.name: EXTERIOR, RAILS, OIL & STORAGE
tasks: Rub the revolver with a lightly oiled cloth; remove the excess but leave a thin protecting film
Remove dust from all crevices with a small, clean brush - the rail slots collect it
Check the rail screws and the grip screw are tight, without re-torquing a mounted optic's mount
Do not keep the revolver in contact with materials that attract moisture, and avoid cloth holsters that retain it
For long storage, take extra care with the metal surfaces against corrosion

reassembly: Nothing came off - the barrel especially - so there is nothing to refit. Let the extractor rod seat fully before the cylinder goes back.

Swing the cylinder home and let BOTH latches engage: the thumb piece at the rear and the front latch on the crane. Feel for the second click; a Raging Hunter with only the rear latch engaged is not closed.
Rotate the closed cylinder by hand through a full turn and confirm it indexes and locks at each of the six stops.
fncheck: With all six chambers confirmed empty: the cylinder must latch at BOTH ends - rear thumb piece and front latch - and show no side play; hand rotation should feel the cylinder stop drop into each notch; the transfer bar must stay clear of the firing pin until the trigger goes fully through and drop back as it returns; and both single and double action should reset positively. Check the barrel/cylinder gap is even as the cylinder turns, and if a scope is mounted on the top rail, confirm its screws are still tight before firing - .44 Magnum recoil finds anything loose in a handful of rounds.
